title: Effects of single-segment Intacs implantation on visual acuity and corneal topographic indices of keratoconus

groups.description: 42 eyes of 32 patients with keratoconus (contact lens intolerance, clear cornea, maximum keratometry below 58 D, mean keratometry below 55 D, peripheral corneal thickness above 450 µm; age range 19-41 years) treated with femtosecond-assisted single-segment Intacs; prospective interventional case series, single surgeon

series.notes: mean ± SD (column subheaders); K Max defined as maximum keratometry power (table footnote), unit D; the follow-up column is labelled '4 months postoperatively' (Methods: Pentacam repeated at 4 months) while the reported follow-up time was 4.7 ± 0.6 months (range 3.7-5.5 months); the labelled time of 4 months is used; per-visit n not reported separately; device from the Methods: Pentacam (Oculus)

exclusions.what: 'Changes' column of Table 1 (K max. row, R9C4)
exclusions.reason: printed as a reduction (positive numbers for flattening), not a change from baseline; the absolute series with its baseline is used

exclusions.what: P column of Tables 1-2 and the correlations of Table 3
exclusions.reason: p-values and correlation coefficients are not admissible as values

notes: Single-arm study of a standard ring segment (single-segment Intacs) without an investigational agent, so the group is a control
Age group adult: the reported age range is 19-41 years
Table 1 also gives UCVA, BSCVA, subjective refraction spherical equivalent, K1, K2 and Km: visual acuity, refraction and other keratometry, not extracted
Table 2 gives Pentacam indices (ISV, IVA, KI, CKI, IHA, IHD, R min): not extracted
Figures 1-2 show visual acuity and spherical equivalent changes: not extracted
